title: My Bodyguard Is Posing as My Husband

core_axes.inciting_disruption: After Laney privately shows COO Richard Vance that his authorization code sits on four Meridian-chain trust adjustments (ch2) and her apartment is covertly entered, Thorne's fixer Halloway cuts her brake line (ch3 last line, ch5), a hidden physical attack seen by no one, which general counsel Meredith Cho answers in an unminuted room with a Halcyon relocation as a fake married couple.
core_axes.the_bind: Staying visible means a professional killer who already tried once; going under means living as Laney Whitfield beside a stranger under a no-break-character rule, and she will not drop the case because she has demanded to be the one who hands the evidence over.
core_axes.first_irreversible_decision: Ch5: she signs the relocation agreement, giving up her name, apartment, phone number, office presence and friends for an estimated three months, on the stated condition that she finishes the case herself.
core_axes.midpoint_reversal: Ch23-24: a hand-delivered photograph of the house proves the cover is found; Laney overrules Rosa's second relocation, Cole backs her, and they hold a known position while she matches the ninth Thorne payment to Halloway's visitor-log Thursday (ch25).
core_axes.rupture_lowest_point: Ch28-32: after their first night Cole misses the 6 a.m. secure check, costing the warrant 11 days; Rosa removes him (ch29), and two nights later Halloway cuts the power, concusses Reyes and breaks in while Laney is alone.
core_axes.climax_action: Ch40: at Ashcroft's investor reception Laney presents the Meridian chain, badge absence and payment match from the podium, Meredith certifies them on the record, Halloway lunges, Cole blocks him, Laney hits him with a glass award, and FBI agents arrest Halloway and Thorne; heroine-led inside a collectively staged plan.
core_axes.repair_mechanism: Cole's changed acts: a next-day private apology for 'good cover' (ch13); full disclosure of his father's murder and his mother's scream (ch27); telling Rosa in the driveway he will resign and guard Laney unlicensed rather than leave (ch35, Rosa witnesses, Laney overhears); declaring love to Meredith (ch42); leaving field work for a home-every-night training post (ch43); vows before the whole street to stand beside her, not in front (ch51).
core_axes.resolution_epilogue_shape: A 13-chapter post-climax tail (about 20% of the text): statements, Vance's hallway confession, Marion's forgiveness, job offers, giving up the old apartment, buying the house, porch proposal, cemetery visit, engagement party, sentencing four months later, backyard wedding, reception and honeymoon; then a two-years-later epilogue swaps THE WHITFIELDS mat for HART-BENNETT under Marion's approval.

evidence_notes: SOURCE: Drive read_file_content cut off at PDF page 80 (in Chapter 19). The full 198-page PDF came through download_file_content, was decoded and extracted with pdftotext -layout, and paragraphs were rebuilt from indentation. All 53 chapters and the Epilogue were read in full, so evidence_level is FULL_TEXT. Front matter gives the author as 'Briar Salvano' (Copyright 2026). STRUCTURE: dual close third person with labelled POV chapters (Laney 31 plus the Epilogue, Cole 22) in uneven alternation. The climax is ch40, about 79% through. Ch41-53 plus the Epilogue (about 13.6k words) are all denouement. INCITING: the discovery (ch1) comes first, but the event that breaks equilibrium and starts the romance container is the brake-line attack (ch3/5), so inciting_kind is external_blow, with discovery as the precondition. HERO_ERROR: the clearest moment is ch12, when Cole kisses her at the Ortiz party and then retreats with 'That was — for the neighbors. Good cover.' His broader pattern is withholding his father's story and treating safety as the only form of love (ch14, ch27). The ch28 missed check is a lapse, not a value error. REPAIR: dominant is risking_real_loss_on_her_behalf (ch35: 'I'd rather lose my career than lose her'). Secondary shapes are changing_a_structure (ch43 training-program job, home every night) and relinquishing_power_or_control (ch24, ch33, and the vows 'stand beside you rather than in front of you'). CLIMAX STAGING: 400-guest investor reception at the Fairport Regency, with board and press present. Documents are shown on a screen and read aloud. The General Counsel verifies them on the record. The FBI arrests on a warrant signed that morning. A physical scuffle follows. SUPPORT: Rosa (Halcyon owner) is the protocol authority who removes and then reinstates Cole. Priya Nasser (FBI) and Meredith Cho (GC) are co-builders of the case. Marion Castellano (widowed neighbor) is the cover-tester and later the refuge. The Ortizes are the model real marriage. Outcomes per ch50: Thorne 22 years, Halloway 8, Vance 4. CONTINUITY ISSUES IN THE TEXT (descriptive): ch13 says 'nine weeks' when it is about 3 weeks in. Ch34 skips weeks ahead (therapy with Dr. Ashworth) before ch35 returns to the dawn after the break-in. Ch46 mentions the porch proposal before ch47 shows it. Ch7 has the move on a Saturday in April but the Epilogue says 'a March afternoon'. Ch37 says 'Ashcroft & Vance' though the firm is Ashcroft Capital elsewhere. Ch40 says 'Eleven weeks ago' while ch5 estimated three months. ENDING: the closing object is the new HART-BENNETT mat, a callback to the THE WHITFIELDS mat on arrival in ch7, and Laney's last line echoes ch15 ('I used to believe safe meant nobody could get to you'). Final paragraph, verbatim: 'Cole kissed the top of her head, and together they sat in the gathering dusk, two people who had once built an entire life out of a careful, necessary lie and had, slowly, patiently, over two remarkable years, built something infinitely truer in its place — a real home, on a real street, under a real name, exactly where they’d always, without quite knowing it yet, been meant to stay.' Then 'THE END'. HEAT: one on-page sex scene (ch28), sensual but not explicit in its language. The rest is kisses.
